output.overview: Saffire IV–VI studied burning large solid samples, including fabric and PMMA, aboard the Cygnus cargo vehicle after it left the ISS [saffire-iv-vi]. This record is not in the PSI combustion archive; its sample conditions and results were hand-transcribed from cited NASA publications, and no approach description is provided [saffire-iv-vi].
keyTakeaways: The record contains 8 runs involving SIBAL cloth, cotton jersey and several PMMA configurations [saffire-iv-vi].
Five runs are classified as burned on a source-field basis; outcomes for the other 3 are unknown, not evidence of non-burning [saffire-iv-vi].
Oxygen, pressure and flow are recorded for all 8 runs; no run pressures were placed at an assumed nominal value [saffire-iv-vi].
output.habitatRelevance: The real runs span 22–31% oxygen and 7.85–14.5 psi, with flow fixed at 20 cm/s; these ranges do not establish coverage of every oxygen–pressure combination [saffire-iv-vi]. They can inform engineering judgment for cabin conditions within the tested coverage, but do not predict ignition or flame spread or replace NASA flammability standards or certified material testing.
output.caveats: The approach, hypothesis and test dates are missing, 3 outcomes are unavailable, results are preliminary, and the flagged Saffire-VI calorimetry total requires confirmation against a possible copy error [saffire-iv-vi].
